newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah firms, swaps ease in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah firms, swaps ease in late trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate late trading on Wednesday, with swap premiums easing on improved liquidity, dealers said.
They said some operators might have sold a small amount of dollars to the central bank as they managed to accumulate them below the 2,371.0 level in the afternoon.
"I think the amount is small. The spot rate was only briefly trading below the 2,371.0 level," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market was a bit surprised with the central bank's higher fixing this afternoon.
But one Japanese bank dealer said he was in fact anticipating it following the dollar's rise against the yen.
Spot rupiah was at 2,370.95/71.10 at 0915 GMT against an opening of 2,371.75/72.25. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,370.50/70.60 and 2,370.50/70.80, respectively.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,371/2,563 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,371/2,419 on Wednesday, the second time this week.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by four points the previous week.
Dealers said overnight money fell to 10.0 percent from an early high of 13.0 percent, suggesting sufficient liquidity in the money market despite month-end factors.
Dealers said an easing of short-term money helped drive longer-term swap rates lower.
One-month swaps were at 11.50/12.50, two at 23.00/24.00, three at 35.50/36.25 and six at 72.25/73.25 points.
Dealers had said earlier spot rupiah faced upward pressure following overnight buying from New York, but saw lukewarm response from Jakarta as players here focussed on liquidity.
